disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates for bobcat and gray fox are set by Commission rule ('Second Saturday in November – Third Sunday in February'). Always verify current regulations, closed areas, and any emergency changes with NDOW before trapping.

license_summary.trapping_license: A Nevada trapping license is required to take a furbearing mammal by trap, snare, or similar device, or to sell raw furs for profit. Furbearers may also be taken by gun or bow and arrow with only a hunting license, but a trapping license is needed to sell pelts.
license_summary.harvest_questionnaire: All Nevada trapping license holders must complete the mandatory furbearer harvest questionnaire online at ndowlicensing.com between May 1 and May 31, regardless of harvest activity. Failure = one-year license suspension, reversible by completing the questionnaire and paying a $50 fee.
license_summary.trap_visitation: Traps/snares must be visited at least once every other calendar day in the listed congested-area units and at least once each 96 hours elsewhere (see NAC 503.152).
license_summary.trap_registration: Each trap, snare, or similar device must be stamped with the trapper's name and address or registered with the Department ($5 per device).
license_summary.closed_areas: Many areas are closed to trapping (refuges, parks, military ranges, congested areas — see the 2026–2027 NDOW guide pp. 42-43, 'Areas Closed to Hunting and Trapping').

seasons.notes: Season dates are set by Commission rule as 'Second Saturday in November – Third Sunday in February' (Nov 14, 2026 – Feb 21, 2027, per the 2026–2027 NDOW guide). CLOSED to nonresidents (residents only). Any bobcat killed must be personally presented by the harvester to the Department for inspection and have the bobcat seal affixed to the pelt within 10 days after the close of the season; the lower jaw must be saved and given to the Department; a bobcat harvest report form must be completed. Each seal costs $5. A bobcat pelt may not be sold, bartered, traded, purchased, transferred, tanned, shipped out of state, or transported from the state without a seal affixed. No person may possess a bobcat pelt 10 days or more after the close of the season without a Department seal affixed.

sources.notes: NAC 503.025 lists Nevada's complete fur-bearing mammal list WITH scientific names (beaver, bobcat, gray/kit/red fox, mink, muskrat, river otter) — all 8 species in this dataset. NAC 503.152 (trap visitation), 503.150 (trap registration), 503.160 (harvest data/questionnaire), 502.347 (bobcat sealing). Archived HTML locally.

verification.confirmation_notes: The 2026–2027 NDOW Small Game guide was published for the 2026-27 season and prints exact calendar dates for every furbearer season (verified 2026-09-18). NAC 503 was last revised 6/7/2026. Day-of-week checks (America/Los_Angeles): Nov 14, 2026 is Saturday (second Saturday of November 2026) and Feb 21, 2027 is Sunday (third Sunday of February 2027), matching the Commission's 'Second Saturday in November – Third Sunday in February' rule.
known_gaps: Nevada's legal furbearer list is exactly the 8 species in NAC 503.025 — all are modeled; no additional state furbearers exist.
Bobcat and gray fox are closed to nonresidents — modeled as notes, not separate nonresident records; the app should flag nonresident users.
Scientific names use the NAC 503.025 spellings verbatim (Mustela vison, Ondatra zibethica); modern synonyms are noted.
Areas closed to trapping (guide pp. 42-43) are summarized, not enumerated.
Detailed method rules (bait restrictions, steel-leghold spacer requirements, congested-area rules) are summarized in the license summary, not fully modeled.
